title: Learning trumpet, trombone and xylophone
summary: He learned trumpet fingering in a couple of lessons from Brookhoven, and taught himself trombone and xylophone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Who taught you to play trumpet, Peter?

Well the old man Brookhoven, he had a band, he was an old German, you know. And the Brookhoven band, Brass Band, you know. He had a couple of boys play trumpet and one played in the theater, you know. Leo I think his name was, but his daddy, well you see I was a musician already because I was playing violin, but all I wanted to learn was the horn. See I knew the music and everything, see. So I went to him and in a couple of lessons I had the horn down, you see, that was all the lesson. I just wanted to learn the fingering, you know.
Who taught you to play trombone? Hmm? Who taught you to play trombone? Trombone? Myself.

Yeah. Or xylophone and then band. Yeah, let's pick that up. Let's pick it up. Well the xylophone is similar to the piano, you see. If you know the chords on the piano, you can come in there playing the xylophone, because it's just like a piano keyboard, you know. But the trombone, I just took it and I knew the bass cleft and everything, you see. All I get, I learned the positions on the horn and that was all, you see. See, it's just like the violin, it's got seven positions, you know.
